title: Affine Algebraic Sets and Coordinate Rings

items.title: An affine algebraic set in affine space
A zero locus depends only on the generated ideal and its radical
items.strategy: A point annihilates every element of S exactly when it annihilates every finite polynomial combination of elements of S, and f(x)=0 if and only if f(x)^n=0. Therefore V(S), V((S)), and V(sqrt((S))) are the same subset of affine space.

items.title: Zero loci in affine space are the closed sets of the classical Zariski topology
items.strategy: Arbitrary intersections are built into the definition of V(S). For finite unions, a point lies in V(IJ) exactly when every product fg vanishes there, which is equivalent to lying in V(I) or V(J); the unit and zero ideals provide the empty and whole-space edge cases.

items.title: The vanishing ideal of a subset of affine space
Vanishing ideals and zero loci form a Galois connection
items.strategy: Unwind the definitions: X is contained in V(J) exactly when every polynomial in J vanishes on every point of X, which is exactly the inclusion J subseteq I(X). Applying this equivalence in each direction yields the two closure operators.

items.title: Affine algebraic sets correspond to radical ideals, and irreducible ones to prime ideals
items.strategy: The local Galois connection gives X = V(I(X)) for algebraic sets and J subseteq I(V(J)) for ideals. The cited strong Nullstellensatz upgrades the latter to I(V(J)) = sqrt(J), and the finite-union identity V(ab)=V(a) union V(b) turns irreducibility of an algebraic set into primality of its vanishing ideal.

items.title: A classical affine variety
Irreducibility is equivalent to every pair of nonempty open sets meeting
items.strategy: The complement of a union of two proper closed sets is the intersection of two nonempty open sets, and conversely the complement of a nondense nonempty open set gives such a closed decomposition. This also yields the equivalent dense-open formulation.

items.title: The coordinate ring of an affine algebraic set
A classical affine variety has a domain as its coordinate ring, and conversely
items.strategy: By definition k[X] is the quotient of the ambient polynomial ring by I(X). The published quotient criterion identifies when that quotient is a domain, and the ideal-variety correspondence identifies prime vanishing ideals with irreducible algebraic sets.

items.title: Polynomial functions on an affine algebraic set are exactly its coordinate ring
items.strategy: A polynomial class in k[x_1,...,x_n]/I(X) defines a function on X by evaluation. Two polynomials define the same function exactly when their difference lies in I(X), so quotient classes are precisely the polynomial functions on X.

items.title: A principal open subset of a classical affine variety
Principal opens form a basis for the Zariski topology on an affine variety
items.strategy: Each D_X(f) is the complement of X intersect V(f), so it is open. If U = X minus V(J) and J is generated by f_1,...,f_r, then U is the union of the principal opens D_X(f_i), and the intersection formula D_X(f) intersect D_X(g) = D_X(fg) is immediate from nonvanishing.

items.title: Regular functions on a principal open are the principal localization of the coordinate ring
items.strategy: Send g/f^n in k[X]_f to the function x mapsto g(x)/f(x)^n on D_X(f). Local quotient representatives on a principal-open cover can be cleared to common powers of f by the standard Nullstellensatz gluing argument, quotient-localization compatibility gives the algebra isomorphism, and the empty-open edge case is exactly the criterion that the localized ring collapses to zero.

items.title: A quasi-affine algebraic set
Every affine algebraic set has finitely many irreducible components
items.strategy: Translate the algebraic set to its radical ideal I(X). Noetherianity gives only finitely many minimal primes above that ideal, the ideal-variety correspondence turns them into a finite irredundant union of irreducible closed subsets, and the irreducibility lemma gives uniqueness.

items.title: A reduced affine k-algebra
Affine algebraic sets contravariantly match reduced affine k-algebras
Points of an affine algebraic set correspond to maximal ideals of its coordinate ring
items.strategy: Evaluation at a point of X gives a maximal ideal of k[X]. Conversely, the weak Nullstellensatz identifies every maximal ideal of k[X] with a k-point of the ambient polynomial ring containing I(X), hence with a point of X itself.

items.title: On the affine line, the classical Zariski topology is cofinite
items.strategy: A proper closed subset of A^1 is the zero locus of a nonzero ideal in k[t], hence of a single nonzero polynomial. A nonzero univariate polynomial over a domain has only finitely many roots, so every proper closed subset is finite.

items.title: Every nonempty open subset of an affine variety is dense
items.strategy: In an irreducible space, every pair of nonempty open subsets meets. If a nonempty open set were not dense, its complement would contain a nonempty open set disjoint from it, contradicting the irreducibility criterion.

items.title: The classical affine dictionary forgets nilpotents and non-rational points

title: Affine Algebraic Sets and Coordinate Rings — Examples

items.title: Affine space has zero vanishing ideal and polynomial coordinate ring
items.strategy: A nonzero polynomial over the infinite field k cannot vanish on every point of k^n, so I(A^n_k)=0. The coordinate-ring definition then identifies k[A^n_k] with the ambient polynomial ring, and the case n=0 reduces to the one-point affine space.

items.title: The parabola y=x^2 has coordinate ring k[t] and isomorphic intrinsic geometry to the affine line
items.strategy: Quotient k[x,y] by the relation y-x^2 and eliminate y by substitution. The resulting map from k[t] to the quotient sends t to the class of x, and the inverse sends the class of y to t^2.

items.title: The coordinate cross V(xy) is reducible and its coordinate ring has zero divisors
items.strategy: Use the union formula V(xy)=V(x) union V(y) to decompose the zero locus into the two coordinate axes. In the quotient ring k[x,y]/(xy), the images of x and y are nonzero but multiply to zero.

items.title: The punctured affine line is a principal open with Laurent-polynomial coordinate ring but is not closed in affine space
items.strategy: Identify A^1 minus {0} with D(t). The principal-open theorem gives its regular-function ring as k[t]_t = k[t,t^{-1}], and the cofinite description of the affine-line Zariski topology shows that removing one point is open but not closed.

items.title: The Zariski topology on the affine line over an infinite field is not Hausdorff
items.strategy: On A^1, every nonempty open set is the complement of a finite set. Over an infinite field the union of two finite sets is still proper, so any two nonempty opens meet and no two distinct points admit disjoint neighborhoods.

items.title: The ideals (x) and (x^2) have the same zero locus but different quotient rings
items.strategy: The zero-locus lemma gives V(x)=V(x^2). But the quotients k[x]/(x) and k[x]/(x^2) differ because the second still contains a nonzero nilpotent class.

items.title: The empty affine algebraic set corresponds to the unit ideal and the zero coordinate ring
items.strategy: By convention V(1)=emptyset. The vanishing ideal of the empty set is the whole polynomial ring, so the coordinate ring is the quotient by the unit ideal, namely the zero ring.
